Per line: speed (× the speaker's), pre/post (ms of silence before/after the voice), say (what is spoken, if not `text`), estVoice (s: the predicted voice length, tools/estimate.py; replaced by the real voice once tools/voice.py has run).

source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI), Adi Parva, Adivamshavatarana sub-parva. CHECKED AGAINST CE 1.57.1–56: King Uparichara Vasu, of Puru's line, takes the land of Chedi on Indra's word (1.57.1–2); Indra gives him a great crystal sky-going car (sphatika vimana), so that he alone of mortals moves above (1.57.13–14, 31), the unfading garland and the bamboo staff (1.57.15, 17); his wife Girika tells him her season has come (1.57.36); that day his ancestors bid him hunt (1.57.37); hunting, he thinks only of her (1.57.38); his seed falls and he catches it on a tree's leaf, lest it and her season be wasted (1.57.39–40); he consecrates it and bids a hawk carry it home to Girika (1.57.42–43); another hawk sees it and attacks, thinking it meat; they fight with their beaks in the air and the seed falls into the Yamuna (1.57.45–46); there the apsara Adrika, turned into a fish by Brahma's curse, swallows it (1.57.47–48: RESOLVED, the curse is Brahma's, brahmashapat; on the plaque as "under a curse"); in the tenth month fishermen catch her and take from her belly a girl and a boy (1.57.49); they report the marvel to the king (1.57.50: `boy`); the king takes the boy, later King Matsya (1.57.51); the apsara, freed by bearing two human children, as foretold, leaves the fish's form and goes the way of the perfected (1.57.52–53); the girl, who smells of fish, the king gives to a fisherman (dasha: 1.57.54; the CE does not call him a chief here); she is Satyavati (1.57.55); to serve her father she plies a boat on the water, and Parashara, on pilgrimage, sees her (1.57.56: the cliffhanger; the CE says he saw her, not that he boarded her boat). Mother of the poet: 1.57.69–71, 1.54.2. The names Indra, Girika, Adrika and Matsya are on plaques, not spoken. The words "his seed" are the text's own and are said once, plainly.
structure: From episode 41 (the step-up; script/ARC-41-50.md): COLD OPEN (≤ 8 words, spoken by ≤ 2.8 s; the hook style rotates and never repeats the episode before) → title (hook post) → STORY from ≈ 4.5 s with the UNVOICED recap band → the episode stands alone (every name has an identifier in "names", shown as a plaque) → one question closed (loop.answeredBy), the previous one answered by 15 s (loop.prevAnsweredBy) → turn at 40–60 % after a real silence, a second silence where the story allows → one face close-up with a change of emotion → one signature shot → the cliffhanger with the source line → a ≤ 1.2 s NEXT › band that dissolves into frame 1. Per line: pal (the colour script: no hue for more than two lines), cam (≥ 4 distinct moves), tr (transitions born from the medium), amb / foley / music (three sound layers; ambLead / ambLag = J- and L-cuts). Gate: tools/gate.mjs.

names.Adrika: an apsara, a nymph of heaven, under a curse

loop.hookQuestion: Why was a girl found inside a fish?
loop.prevQuestion: Why does the full story begin with a king, a fish and a ferry girl?
loop.openQuestion: Which sage came to Satyavati's river?

strings.episodeTitle: The King, the Fish and the Ferry Girl
strings.prevEpisodeTitle: The Whole Story in One Breath
strings.recapLine: To tell the whole Mahabharata, the teller went back to its beginning.

lines.text: Why was a girl found inside a fish?
lines.say: Why was a girl [p:80] found inside a fish?
lines.note: COLD OPEN (a question card over the image): under the river's surface, a great silver fish turning in a shaft of light, a pearl glow in her side; a net coming down from above. The card in the upper water.

lines.text: It begins with the poet's grandfather: Uparichara, a king with a crystal chariot of the sky.
lines.say: It begins with the poet's grandfather: [p:200] Uparichara, [p:80] a king with a crystal chariot [p:60] of the sky.
lines.note: STORY 0 with the unvoiced recap band (top) · NEW LIGHT (crystal-sky): a lamp-glow match cut from the pearl to the sun: a chariot like cut glass crossing bright cloud, the king in royal blue and gold (plaques: Uparichara · king of Chedi; small: a gift of Indra). Pays off episode 48's last line by 5 s.

lines.text: Out hunting, he longed for his queen.
lines.say: Out hunting, [p:120] he longed for his queen.
lines.note: STORY 1 · NEW LIGHT, the forest in spring (hunt-emerald, petals) · THE CLOSE-UP: the king's face under blossom: the hunter's set brow softens (resolve to tenderness), his eyes go far; in the petals, the faint shape of the queen (plaque: Girika · his queen).

lines.text: He sealed his seed in a leaf, and sent it home with a hawk.
lines.say: He sealed his seed in a leaf, [p:150] and sent it home [p:60] with a hawk.
lines.note: STORY 2: his two hands fold a broad leaf into a packet and tie it (hands and leaf only); a hawk on his wrist takes it; a crane up with the hawk through the canopy into the open.

lines.text: Over the river Yamuna, a rival hawk struck. The leaf fell.
lines.say: Over the river Yamuna, [p:100] a rival hawk struck. [p:350] The leaf fell.
lines.note: STORY 3: two hawks tumbling against the bright sky; the green packet drops; a tilt down with it, cloud, air, the river's blue surface coming up (plaque: Yamuna · the river).

lines.text: A fish swallowed it: an apsara under a curse.
lines.say: A fish swallowed it: [p:250] an apsara [p:60] under a curse.
lines.note: STORY 4 · THE SIGNATURE SHOT: under water: the focus racks from drifting weed in the foreground to the great silver fish rising to the sinking leaf; as she turns, for a moment her shadow on the river bed is a woman's with a diadem (plaque: Adrika · an apsara, a nymph of heaven, under a curse).

lines.text: Ten months later, fishermen opened that fish, and found two children.
lines.say: Ten months later, [p:100] fishermen opened that fish, [p:250] and found two children.
lines.note: STORY 5 · THE TURN (≈ 50 %) after a real silence · NEW LIGHT, the fishers' shore at dusk (fishers-coral): nets, boats; the fisher chief kneeling, his face lit from below by a soft light in the basket before him: weary to wonder; two small bright heads. Answers the hook. (No knife, no wound: the light opens.)

lines.text: The king kept the boy. The apsara, freed, rose to heaven.
lines.say: The king kept the boy. [p:200] The apsara, [p:60] freed, [p:60] rose to heaven.
lines.note: STORY 6: fishermen at the palace steps with the two children (they took them to the king: seen, not said); the king lifts a boy (plaque: Matsya · the boy, later a king); a tilt up from them through pearl mist: the fish's silver skin falls back into the water and a luminous woman rises, not touching the ground.

lines.text: The girl smelled of fish. He gave her to a fisherman.
lines.say: The girl smelled of fish. [p:200] He gave her [p:60] to a fisherman.
lines.note: STORY 7: the fisherman receives the small girl in both arms (offer, then carry: an eased blend) and turns away with her along the shore, past the hanging nets; a lateral track.

lines.text: Her name was Satyavati: one day, mother of the poet himself.
lines.say: Her name [p:60] was Satyavati: [p:250] one day, [p:80] mother of the poet himself.
lines.note: STORY 8 (a second real silence before it): years in one orbit: the child, a girl, a young woman with an oar, standing in the stern of a boat (plaque: Satyavati · a fisherman's daughter); behind her, faint in the dusk, the tall haloed figure of episode 47 (answers episode 48's question: this is where the poet comes from).

lines.text: She grew up rowing a ferry, until a great sage came to the river.
lines.say: She grew up rowing a ferry, [p:150] until a great sage [p:80] came to the river.
lines.note: NEXT 1 (the catalog's cliffhanger): the river in lavender mist: her boat at the bank, she small in its stern; on the bank path, back to us and far from her, a tall sage with a staff stops and looks out over the water (the text: he saw her as she plied the boat). The source line (top).
The NEXT › band over the cliffhanger image, with the source line; dissolve into frame 1.
